newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling up on reduced importer demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling up on reduced importer demand.

text.p: Reduced importer demand helped the Kenyan shilling firm against the dollar on Thursday, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 55.40 against the dollar from 55.42 on Wednesday. On the pound, it was posted at 93.04 from 92.75.
Dealers said inflows from exporter sales streamed steadily into the market. Horticulture inflows helped undermine the dollar strength.
On Wednesday, some dealers thought that intervention from the central bank would cap the shilling's gain.
"Despite some dollar buying interest from the central bank, the shilling strengthened, as they bought only small amounts at the levels of 55.42 and 55.43," one dealer said.
Another dealer said he expected the shilling to strengthen on dollars coming in from tea and coffee exporters.
The money market was very liquid with many banks lending. Rates were quoted between five percent and 12 percent from 10 percent levels on Wednesday.
